title: Search engines: Elasticsearch, OpenSearch and Solr

videos.script: A customer types café torrado into Quitanda's search box. A database can find rows that contain those exact letters. It cannot tell that cafés, cafe and torrada are the same words, or which of forty matches the customer most likely meant. {{database}} That is a different job, and it has its own kind of system: the search engine. {{engine}} Elasticsearch, OpenSearch and Solr are the three you will meet. All three are built on the same library, Lucene, and they share most of their ideas. {{lucene}} On your machine you will run OpenSearch beside Quitanda's database, and feed it a copy of the catalogue, because a search index is a copy and never the source of truth. {{copy}} You will see what the engine does to a word before it stores it, why a misspelt search still finds coffee, and how results are ranked. {{analysis}} And you will search for a product the moment after adding it, and not find it. {{refresh}} This is the heaviest lab after lesson 10. It needs about a gigabyte and a half of memory while it runs.
